A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIS method and TRM policy-improvement interpretation despite the changed title. All pages, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original N-Queens and ARC experiments, training-time measurements, and a comparison of diffusion-generated and LLM-generated supervision targets.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments, including the target-generator comparison in Appendix C, and reports revised ARC scores in Table 1.

M1.justification: DIS retains the same shared backbone, intermediate-target cross-entropy objective, corruption schedule, timestep conditioning, detached recursion, and fixed six-step procedure without halting. The pseudocode is unchanged and moves to Appendix A; the policy-improvement reformulation does not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use 8-by-8 N-Queens, ARC-AGI-1, ARC-AGI-2, and ConceptARC training puzzles. V1 mentions Sudoku-Extreme but supplies no separate experiment, so its omission does not establish removed evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same six pretrained LLM comparators and the TRM, TRM-medium, and TRM-compact rows. The Gemini 2.5 Pro target-generation comparison also remains, moving from v1 Section 6 to v3 Appendix C.

E3.justification: Documented protocols remain unchanged: 7,200 training and 200 test N-Queens examples, ARC pass@2 with 1,000 augmentations, the same model sizes, and the same recursion and optimization settings. No revised protocol is specified for the changed Table 1 scores.

E4.justification: The compact/medium comparisons, learning curves, integer-versus-continuous timestep finding, and alternative-target-generator experiment are retained. The latter still reports 10% accuracy with LLM-generated targets versus 24% with diffusion targets, now in Appendix C. No new robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars for the original experiments. The retained plots use the same single-curve reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes DIS-medium ARC-2 from 3.0 to 2.5 and TRM ARC-2 from 3.0 to 3.3. The unqualified DIS row changes from 40.0/3.0 to 41.3/6.0 on ARC-1/ARC-2, placing it above TRM on both. Other reported findings remain unchanged. These are revised reported scores; neither corrections nor reruns are explained.

T1.justification: V3 introduces explicit MDP, occupancy, and KL-regularized objective formulations, removes v1 Appendix A.2's Lyapunov contraction and hitting-time proposition, and replaces the guaranteed-improvement proof with a five-step concentration argument in Appendix B. The original advantage-margin derivative criterion survives in Section 3.3, rather than constituting a new theorem.

C1.justification: The policy-improvement interpretation, DIS contribution, 18-fold forward-pass reduction, and 24% compact-model ARC result remain. V3 narrows the introduction's state-of-the-art performance claim to competitive performance and adds an abstract-level claim that recursive layers can contribute ineffective computation relative to matched feed-forward depth.

C2.justification: V3 adds a substantive critique of effective-depth and fixed-point explanations, discussing non-negligible latent residuals and interpreting useful recursion through task-aligned policy updates. The fixed-step limitation and explanation that nonlinear LLM-generated trajectories hinder small models remain essentially unchanged in Appendix C.

D1.justification: Backbone details, model widths, optimizer parameters, warm-up, corruption sampling, and timestep conditioning are retained. Both report four H100 GPUs and approximately 40 versus 72 training hours. Pseudocode is relocated without procedural changes, and no new code or data access information appears.

R1.justification: V3 adds Bai et al. on Deep Equilibrium Models and positions its explanation against fixed-point accounts. It removes the GPT-4o, OpenAI o1, and Chain-of-Thought references by Hurst, Jaech, and Wei respectively. The central relationships to TRM, HRM, and Frans et al.'s guidance-based policy improvement remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of Sections 2.3–4 are rewritten around policy improvement and ineffective recursion. The theoretical exposition is reorganized, discussion moves to Appendix C, and appendices are restructured into illustrations, proofs, and discussion. Template running headers are replaced with the paper title.

P2.justification: V1's corruption illustrations in Figures 1 and 7 are removed. Its architecture diagram and pseudocode move to Appendix A as v3 Figures 5 and 4. The unchanged N-Queens and ARC graphics are repositioned or resized, including removal of text wrapping around the N-Queens curve, and Table 1 loses its colored cell highlighting.

improvement.justification: V3 improves organization and narrows the performance claim, but its replacement for v1's heuristic improvement proof does not clearly resolve the theoretical gap. Appendix B claims concentration even at guidance weight zero, although that leaves the reference policy unchanged, and establishes the final-target conclusion only at the last step. Revised ARC scores are unexplained, while useful corruption illustrations disappear. These mixed changes do not establish a reliable net improvement in overall quality.
